beats.says: Six acceptors stand in a grid of 2 rows and 3 columns. A majority would need 4 of 6 for each write. The grid uses one shape to elect and another shape to write.
Node 0 starts an election. Phase 1 needs a promise from one acceptor of every column.
The promises cover the three columns, so node 0 is the leader.
Slot 0 belongs to column 0: nodes 0 and 3. Node 0 votes for itself and sends the Accept to node 3 only.
The full column voted, so alpha is chosen. Two acceptors of six did the work.
Slot 1 belongs to column 1: nodes 1 and 4. A second write touches two other nodes.
Now choose a case.

choices.label: Two quorums that do not meet
Elect with half the nodes down
A node of a column is down
Move a stuck slot to another column
The leader dies after a write

beats.says: Five nodes, and each one is an acceptor. Each phase waits for a majority: 3 of 5.
Node 0 starts an election. Its Prepares to nodes 3 and 4 are lost.
Nodes 1 and 2 promise. With its own promise, node 0 has 3 of 5, so it leads.
A client writes alpha at slot 0. The Accepts to nodes 3 and 4 are lost too.
Nodes 0, 1 and 2 vote: 3 of 5. alpha is chosen, and only these three nodes know it.
Now nodes 0 and 1 crash. Of the three nodes that voted, only node 2 is up.
Node 4 starts an election. Nodes 2, 3 and 4 are up: just a majority.
Two majorities of five always share a node. Here it is node 2, and its promise reports alpha.
So node 4 proposes alpha again at slot 0. Nodes 2, 3 and 4 vote, and alpha stays chosen.
Two nodes of five are down, and writes go on. A client writes bravo at slot 1.
Now node 3 crashes too. Only nodes 2 and 4 are up: 2 of 5, less than a majority.
A client writes charlie. Only nodes 2 and 4 can vote, so charlie waits.
No vote is lost. Node 3 restarts, and node 4 sends its open Accepts again.
Node 3 votes, and charlie is chosen. A majority of 5 nodes survives 2 failures.

beats.says: Six acceptors stand in a grid of 2 rows and 3 columns. A majority would be 4 of 6.
The grid has two shapes. To elect: one node of every column. To write: one full column.
Node 0 starts an election. Its Prepares to nodes 3, 4 and 5 are lost.
Nodes 1 and 2 promise. With node 0, that is one node of each column, so node 0 leads.
Slot 0 belongs to column 0: nodes 0 and 3. A client writes alpha, and node 3 votes.
The full column voted, so alpha is chosen. Two acceptors of six did the work.
Why is it safe? A full column holds one node of every election quorum.
So a later leader always hears from a node of the column that chose alpha.
Now node 4 crashes. It is one of the two nodes of column 1.
Slot 1 belongs to column 1. A client writes bravo, but node 4 cannot vote, so bravo waits.
The leader moves slot 1 to column 2: the same ballot and the same value, to nodes 2 and 5.
A node down stops the slots of its column only. The other columns go on.
Partitions are another shape: a majority of one partition writes, a majority of each elects.
A grid writes to few acceptors. The price: each election must ask every column.
